name: LPmud 2.4.5
english_description: A pristine, pre-LDMud LPMud 2.4.5 snapshot -- the mudlib distributed with Lars Pensjo's own original LPMud driver line, from right before the LDMud/MudOS fork. Zero driver_hook usage anywhere, unlike the LDMud-ported Docker Hub ldmuddev/lp245 image of nominally the same version. A real, playable small world (286 files, hundreds of rooms, NPCs, a level/experience system) rather than an infrastructure sketch. The most severe finding was a genuine infinite-recursion bug present in the original 1990s source itself: room/room.lpc's shared 'number word' cache used file_name(this_object())=="room/room" to detect its own singleton instance, but this driver's file_name() always returns a leading slash, so the comparison was always false and the singleton called itself forever -- breaking every room's long-form exit description in the whole game, with the driver's own default-error-message config masking the crash from ordinary players even though debug.log logged it in full every time. A second severe finding: obj/player.lpc called move_player() -- the function every single movement in the game funnels through -- but never defined it and inherits nothing; the real implementation existed verbatim-compatible in the separate, never-wired-up obj/living.lpc.
